clue.text: In Africa it flows down meandering line

indicators.note: a meandering course wanders and winds, so the word that follows is rearranged

blocks.note: feeling down means feeling blue
the letters of line, rearranged

explanation.surface: A geography question about a river that winds its way downstream across Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase: 'In Africa it flows' describes the BLUE NILE, and 'down' looks like the direction of flow but means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blue Nile is a river rising in Ethiopia that joins the White Nile at Khartoum.

blocks.note: surface reading: a sensational article printed in a periodical
setter's reading: what a gun's magazine is loaded with, namely cartridges

explanation.surface: A tabloid magazine runs a sensational, explosive story.
explanation.walkthrough: A magazine is also the chamber of a firearm or a store for munitions, so its explosive content is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammo is the informal word for ammunition, the cartridges loaded into a gun's magazine.

indicators.note: uncontrolled letters run wild and fall out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A learner driver's frenzy gets out of hand and they turn violent.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal, used of a person, is a brute or savage lacking civilised restraint.

clue.text: We British following horse and trap

indicators.note: following places what comes before it after the next item, so the order is reversed from the clue

blocks.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
taken as written
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: We British turn up behind a horse and a two-wheeled carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse and trap' suggests a pony and carriage, but 'and' is only a link and the trap is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobweb is the net a spider spins to catch and trap insects.

clue.text: Spouse no longer covered bust, one admitted

indicators.note: something admitted is let inside, so it goes into the other letters
something bust is broken apart, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A former partner covered up a sculpted bust after someone was let in.
explanation.definitionFit: A divorcee is a person whose marriage has been legally ended, so no longer a husband or wife.

clue.text: Excluding line from fashion causes visual problem

indicators.note: excluding something means leaving it out of the word that follows

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line
a style is a fashion

explanation.surface: A designer's rule: dropping a line from the collection leads to an eyesore.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, an eye complaint.

blocks.note: ruddy and flaming are both mild British swear words, and both mean red
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher corrects someone who called a bird a ruddy duck: it is actually a wading bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The ruddy duck is a real species, which makes the surface plausible; and the answer is itself ruddy, being a pink bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A flamingo is a long-legged pink bird that feeds standing in shallow water, a classic wader.

clue.text: Greek character is out tracing Achaean origins

indicators.note: the origins of words are where they start, their opening letters

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: A Greek figure sets off to trace their ancient Achaean ancestry.
explanation.walkthrough: The Achaeans were Homer's name for the ancient Greeks, which ties the surface together.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet.

blocks.note: RE is religious education, the British school subject
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A pupil's behaviour got better in a religious studies lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is Religious Education, a subject in British schools; 'Bible class' reads as one idea but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A reform is a change made to put something right, so a betterment.

blocks.note: W is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a wide
a hole is something dug out

explanation.surface: A broad dig has been finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole means entire, with nothing missing.

blocks.note: first meaning: someone highly skilled
second meaning: in tennis, a serve the opponent cannot touch

explanation.surface: A tennis pro's serve cannot be returned.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is both a highly skilled person and, in tennis, a serve that wins the point outright.

clue.text: Sidearm having first round in place

indicators.note: in tells us these pieces sit inside the word that follows

blocks.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
1ST written with I for 1
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A holstered gun with its first bullet already chambered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' tempts as a bullet in this gun scene, but it is just the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistol is a handgun, the weapon worn at the side.

blocks.note: top means chief or leading
a heavy is a hired tough

explanation.surface: The chief heavy in a gang is in some way mentally unsteady.
explanation.walkthrough: The adverb before the definition looks like an anagram signal, but no letters move: principal and thug simply join end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-heavy describes something with too much weight above, so it is liable to topple over.

indicators.note: beyond places the first word further along, after the second

blocks.note: a beck is a northern English word for a brook
a machine that is functioning is on

explanation.surface: A working signal light on the far side of a brook.
explanation.walkthrough: A beck is a small stream in the dialect of northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To beckon is to gesture to someone to come nearer, a verb of signalling.

indicators.note: ripped means torn up, so the letters are pulled apart and reordered

blocks.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: An onlooker watches as a vicar's vestment is torn.
explanation.walkthrough: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: An observer is someone who watches attentively without taking part.

blocks.note: surface reading: a fermenting bin for making beer at home
setter's reading: the pot in which tea is brewed in every household

explanation.surface: Equipment for the amateur who makes beer in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: Tea is said to brew as it steeps, so domestic brewing needs no beer at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A teapot is the lidded pot in which tea leaves steep in hot water.

clue.text: Thus far the lonely heart's desire?

blocks.note: first meaning: up until now
second meaning: a single person wants someone to go out with

explanation.walkthrough: Lonely hearts are the personal ads where single people seek a partner; read as 'to date', what they want.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means up to the present as an adverb, and literally names the wish to go on dates.

indicators.note: devouring means swallowing, so one part goes inside the other

blocks.note: 3-down's answer is animal, and an animal is a beast
R is the chess notation for a rook

explanation.surface: A savage animal eats a rook and a piece of chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: The 3 refers to the answer to 3-down; a synonym of that answer supplies the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: The breast is the white-meat cut from the front of a chicken.

clue.text: Is it smoking jacket that becomes one?

definitions.text: Is it smoking jacket that becomes one?

blocks.clueFragment: Is it smoking jacket that becomes one?
blocks.note: surface reading: a velvet smoking jacket worn by a gentleman

blocks.clueFragment: Is it smoking jacket that becomes one?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a jacket that is on fire and smoking turns into something that blazes

explanation.surface: A query about whether a smoking jacket suits its wearer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Becomes' can mean suits, but here it means turns into; a jacket ablaze is literally a blazer.
explanation.definitionFit: A blazer is a sports or school jacket, and literally anything that is burning brightly.

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
the second and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: Instructions for maintaining an aged gun.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking alternate letters across 'old rifle' together gives nothing; old is abbreviated separately.
explanation.definitionFit: To oil something is to apply lubricant so it moves smoothly.

indicators.note: ousting means throwing out, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: an ally is a friend
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A political ally expels a Republican, a devilish act.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiend is an evil spirit or demon.

clue.text: Chap avoiding pained expression gets cut down

indicators.note: avoiding means steering clear of, so those letters are left out

blocks.note: a fellow is a man
ow is the cry of someone hurt

explanation.surface: A man trying not to wince gets knocked down to size.
explanation.definitionFit: To fell a tree is to chop it down.

indicators.note: woven threads are interlaced, so the letters are intertwined in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of the Spanish region

explanation.surface: Fabric that is produced on looms in the Spanish region of Aragon.
explanation.definitionFit: Angora is a soft fabric made from the hair of the Angora goat or rabbit.

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so one part is held inside the other

blocks.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: A girl catching a pass shows what she means to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ball' and 'goal' sit together in a football picture, but ball is only the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal is an aim or purpose one intends to achieve.

clue.text: Son needing place to go — Ukrainian maybe

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
lav, short for lavatory, is the toilet, where one goes

explanation.surface: A son urgently needs a toilet, perhaps while in Ukraine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place to go' looks like a destination, but it is the British euphemism for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukrainians are one of the Slavic peoples, so a Ukrainian is an example of a Slav.

indicators.note: claims means takes possession of, so one letter is taken inside the rest
an explosion scatters things, so these letters are blown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: A dangerous chemical in a lab claims the life of a young person from the east.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is a young person aged thirteen to nineteen.
